resolution_notes: Retain the Hesiodic and Iliadic witnesses as coexisting source-level variants; do not force a single normalized parentage.
summary: Hesiod’s Theogony narrates Aphrodite arising from the aftermath of Uranus’s castration, while the Iliad names Dione as her mother and elsewhere calls Aphrodite a daughter of Zeus.

resolution_notes: No redirects or alias merges were created. Three EXPLICITLY_DISTINCT identity assessments record the source-bounded separation; additional homonyms may still be discovered.
summary: Three major figures named Perses are now stored separately: the Titan father of Hecate, the son of Helios in Colchian/Tauric mythography, and the son of Perseus and Andromeda in Herodotus.

resolution_notes: Keep separate canonical entities; future diachronic scholarship may add a qualified relationship without automatic identity.

resolution_notes: Keep ancient and modern entities separate and connect them only through modern_adaptations.
summary: Old Norse witnesses make Hel a child of Loki and do not make Loki Thor’s brother; Marvel screen continuity makes Loki an adoptive brother and Hela a half-sister of Thor.

resolution_notes: Add archaeological miniature-axe pendants and comparative scholarship only as low-confidence, separately sourced layers.

resolution_notes: Never merge Baal Hammon, Baalshamin, Melqart, biblical Baalim or other regional figures by name alone.
summary: Baal can be a lord/master title while the Ugaritic Baalu/Haddu dossier refers to a particular storm-deity figure in registered witnesses.

resolution_notes: Keep a canonical composite entity with two component edges and dated evidence.
summary: Amun-Ra involves Amun and Ra but cannot be safely represented as a spelling alias or destructive merge.

summary: Spell 17 identifies Khepri with Ra-Horakhty in one explanation while other witnesses address Khepri independently.

summary: Ra-Horakhty invokes Horus in a horizon-specific scope; a merge into the general Horus record would erase other Horus forms.
